slides.title: Why does a headwind feel so brutal?
slides.sub: Position, stroke and route fixes for windy days

slides.title: The air counts your airspeed
slides.body: Skate at 25 kph into a 15 kph wind and the air pushes back as hard as it would at 40 kph. You do expensive work at a cheap speed.

slides.title: Get low, not just bent
slides.body: Drop your chest towards your thigh, flatten your back and tuck your head in line with it. In a steady headwind, carry one arm on the back.

slides.title: Shorten the stroke, raise the cadence
slides.body: A long, heavily loaded push stalls into wind. Take more pushes per minute, each a little lighter, like dropping into an easier gear.

slides.title: Respect the gaps in a crosswind
slides.body: Wind speeds up through gaps between buildings, walls and flyovers. Ease off on the approach, stay low and leave room on both sides.

slides.text: On a gusty day the wind picks your line.

slides.title: Out into it, home with it
slides.caption: Take the headwind leg first on fresh legs, so the wind helps you home when you are tired.
